evidence: src/application/dtos.ts declares CreateUserInput, CreateProjectInput, CreateTaskInput, TaskFilterInput, UserDto, ProjectDto and TaskDto. These are the inputs and outputs of the TaskManagementService methods.

src/application/task-management-service.ts: the TaskManagementService constructor injects UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository and IdGenerator, and every save and lookup goes through them.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: the private requireProject(id) is the only project-existence check, used by both createTask and listProjectTasks.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: the private toTaskDto(task) is the only Task-to-TaskDto conversion, used by createTask, listProjectTasks and markTaskDone.
src/application/task-management-service.ts: markTaskDone calls the domain method task.markDone() instead of setting the status itself.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module passes. It is one cohesive application-layer unit for task management. dtos.ts holds the input and output types for the use cases. task-management-service.ts implements those use cases with the DTOs, the domain entities, and the repository and IdGenerator ports injected through the constructor. It never goes around these abstractions: all persistence goes through the injected repositories, and every ID comes from IdGenerator. Each check is defined once and reused. Project existence is checked only in requireProject, which createTask and listProjectTasks both call. Task-to-DTO conversion lives only in toTaskDto, which createTask, listProjectTasks and markTaskDone all call. Marking a task done is delegated to the domain method Task.markDone instead of being repeated here. The due-date check in createTask converts the input text into a date, which belongs in the application layer. One small inconsistency: createUser and createProject build their DTOs inline instead of using helpers like toTaskDto. Each of those conversions appears only once, so nothing is duplicated, and this is too minor to count as a violation.
